# Google Is Adding New Gemini Tools for Small Business Owners

> **In short:** Google says it is announcing new tools for Gemini, its AI assistant, including a dedicated business landing page. The company says the goal is to help small business owners around the world. The announcement includes specific tools for connecting apps, creating brand visuals, and analyzing finances.

If you run a shop, a small office, or a one-person service, you already know how many small jobs pile up: replies to customers, product descriptions, schedules, and social posts. Google's latest update is aimed at that kind of work.

## What was announced

Google says it is launching new tools for Gemini. Gemini is Google's AI assistant, a chatbot you type to or speak with to get help writing, researching, and planning. (A chatbot is a program that answers in plain language, the way a person would in a chat window.)

The announcement also mentions a dedicated business landing page. A landing page is a web page built for one specific purpose, and in this case it points small business owners to Gemini's business-focused content and features. Google describes the whole update as a way to help small business owners "around the world," so it is not limited to one country.

## What the tools do

The announcement describes several specific features:

- **Connect apps**: You can link Gemini to Google tools like Google Business Profile, Google Ads, and Google Workspace, as well as third-party apps like Shopify, Canva, Dropbox, Wix, Zoho, Xero, and Adobe.

- **Brand visuals**: Businesses can upload their website, brand kit, fonts, or color palettes to define their brand style. Gemini uses a model called Nano Banana 2.1 to generate consistent, professional visuals for marketing campaigns. Gemini remembers this style so you do not have to upload guidelines repeatedly.

- **Financial insights**: Gemini can turn messy spreadsheets, receipts, and purchase records into clear financial graphics and interactive models in seconds.

The tools are beginning to roll out in the coming days globally for all Gemini app users.

## How to think about it

Even without the full details, you can prepare. Ask yourself which tasks take the most time each week. Common examples include:

- Drafting emails and replies to customers
- Writing product or service descriptions
- Planning social media posts
- Summarizing long documents, like supplier contracts or reports

Make a short list of these tasks now. When the tools arrive, you will know exactly what to test first.

## What this means for you

- **For your business**: If AI tools are already part of your daily work, keep an eye on whether the new Gemini tools cover the tasks on your list. Test them on low-risk work first, such as drafting a post, before using them for anything with money or customer data.
- **If you're just getting started**: You don't need to act yet. Pick one repetitive task you do every week and write down how long it takes you. That gives you a baseline to measure against later.
- **In everyday life**: If you run a side business or sell things online, the same idea applies. Use an AI assistant to draft, then check and edit the result yourself before it goes out under your name.

## Wrap-up

Google says it is adding new tools to Gemini and launching a dedicated business landing page to help small business owners around the world. The tools include connecting to apps, creating on-brand visuals using Nano Banana 2.1, and turning spreadsheets into financial insights. They are rolling out globally in the coming days. Today, make your list of the three to five small tasks that eat your time. When the tools become available, you will be ready to try them on the work that matters most to you.
